stories.title: Inflation falls to 14.06 percent, but prices still rising
stories.body: The National Bureau of Statistics said headline inflation fell to 14.06 percent in October 2026, from 14.63 percent in September and 18.97 percent a year earlier. Food inflation was 19.13 percent. Month on month, prices rose 0.43 percent, up from 0.06 percent in September. Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele said falling inflation does not mean falling prices, only that prices are rising more slowly.
stories.why: Knowing the latest inflation figure, and the difference between inflation and prices, is a common economy question.

cards.front: What was Nigeria's headline inflation in October 2026 (NBS)?
cards.back: 14.06 percent, down from 14.63 percent in September.

cards.front: Does falling inflation mean prices are falling?
cards.back: No. It means prices are rising more slowly. Falling prices is called deflation.

stories.title: Ukraine, US and Europe to meet in Berlin; Russia objects
stories.body: President Zelenskyy said online talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and European representatives were not easy, and that the next meeting will be in Berlin with the Coalition of the Willing. Kushner said a final agreement will require difficult decisions. The Kremlin said it had not agreed to widen the talks to Europe, and no date was set for a new round with Russia. Drone and missile strikes by both sides continue.
stories.why: Disagreement over who sits at the table is slowing the path to a ceasefire.

cards.front: What is the 'Coalition of the Willing' in the Ukraine war?
cards.back: A group of mainly European countries backing Ukraine and planning post-war security guarantees.

stories.title: Bandits attack mosque in Zamfara during dawn prayers
stories.body: Suspected bandits attacked the Lowcost Mosque in Kaura Namoda town, Zamfara State, during dawn prayers, killing APC e-registration supervisor Nasiru Sani and abducting an unconfirmed number of worshippers. In October, bandits attacked the same town for over three hours, killing seven Joint Task Force members and abducting 38 residents.
stories.why: Repeated attacks on the same town show how bandits are able to strike even inside towns in Zamfara.

stories.title: Trump: 'We don't need a deal with Iran'
stories.body: President Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran and told Vice-President Vance, who had led negotiations, to focus on domestic issues. Secretary of State Rubio said economic pressure on Iran is working and will get worse, so large-scale military operations are unnecessary. Iran says it has sent a seven-condition proposal through Qatar and that the ball is in the US court. On the same day, Iran claimed it struck a US radar site in Bahrain; the US said it shot down two Iranian drones and nothing was damaged.
stories.why: A long 'no war, no peace' stand-off keeps Hormuz disrupted and oil prices high, which shapes Nigeria's revenue and fuel costs.

cards.front: How did Chatham House describe the US–Iran situation in November 2026?
cards.back: "No war, no peace": neither a deal nor full-scale fighting.

stories.title: Herzog asks Eisenkot to form Israel's next government
stories.body: President Isaac Herzog tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government after the 27 October election. Eisenkot's alliance won 48 seats and Netanyahu's bloc 53, both short of 61. Eisenkot has six weeks and said he is open to including Netanyahu. He has ruled out relying on Arab-led parties, which won a record 19 seats. Netanyahu stays caretaker prime minister.
stories.why: A change of Israeli government could affect the Gaza ceasefire and the war with Iran.

cards.front: Who was asked to form Israel's government in November 2026?
cards.back: Gadi Eisenkot, given six weeks by President Herzog.
